summary: Iteration 13 validates the new image-analysis correction (imaging.keystone + white_balance + correct_crop + correct_page) and the pipeline wiring (page.corrected / keystone flags, image_url re-upload, OCR on corrected image). All 15 executed tests in /app/backend/tests/test_imaging.py pass (11 unit + 4 real-AI). UNIT TestKeystone — 1600x2000 dark (60,50,40) background with yellowish paper quad [(300,250),(1300,350),(1400,1800),(200,1700)] (TL,TR,BR,BL as y/x normalised 0-1000) yields a warped image 1200x1450 (within tolerance 1150-1260 x 1400-1500 per the max-distance formula in imaging._coeffs/dist); the four 10-pixel corner pixels of the output read as paper colour (R>150 & G>140 & B>100 after BICUBIC softening). Frame corners [[0,0],[0,1000],[1000,1000],[1000,0]] return None (early exit). Non-convex / inverted order (TL right of TR) returns None (convexity gate). Paper covering <25% of each axis returns None (sanity gate). Bad types (None, [], short list, string) return None. UNIT TestWhiteBalance — pure (235,220,170) 400x400 after white_balance has median [245,245,244] all channels (>=244 within 1 rounding step of the 245 target in the code). (20,15,10) 300x300 is returned bit-for-bit identical (min<60 bypass). UNIT TestCorrectCrop — crop (400,500,700,800) from 1000x1200 yellowish page returns an image of exactly (300,300), near-edge crop (0,0,100,100) returns (100,100). UNIT TestCorrectPage — no corners => wb only, output is a valid JPEG (SOI FFD8FF), preserves 600x800 size and median>=240; frame corners => no warp but size preserved. REAL AI (test_02 skewed JPEG + test_03 straight PDF + test_04 rescan = 3 paid Gemini-fast page runs; test_02 one re-run during rescan still only RE-reads OCR, no corner call because corrected=true already): 1800x2400 skewed JPEG (dark random noise 40-80 bg + yellowish paper quad + 6 Swedish text lines + red pictogram) uploaded via /api/uploads/* -> status=done, page.corrected=true, page.keystone=true (ai.detect_page_corners returned corners and keystone warped), (width,height) changed from upload 1800x2400 to the warped dimensions, image_url re-uploaded to CommHub (differs from the initial upload), markdown length >= 20. Straight white PDF page uploaded -> status=done, page.corrected=true, page.keystone=false (corner detector returned None for is_photo_of_page=false), markdown contains recognisable Swedish text (e.g. 'sida'/'rak'/'test'). Rescan via POST /api/pages/{id}/rescan triggered pipeline.enqueue with rescan=true -> page re-ran OCR, status back to done; crucially the correction branch was SKIPPED because page.corrected was already true (pipeline.py:202 `if not page.get('corrected')`) -> page.image_url is UNCHANGED (asserted equality against stored prev url), corrected stays true. Settings pinned speed_mode=fast + primary_provider=gemini pre- and post-test. Frontend smoke on 390x844: CopyThat login (test@copythat.app / 246810) succeeds, Archive renders, TEST_IMG_FE_Course -> TEST_IMG_FE_Doc opens, 'Visa original' button toggles to 'Dölj original' and shows an whose src is the CommHub-stored CORRECTED page image (https://d2uopk0rz2xy0j.cloudfront.net/.../images/…) — no red-screen, no pageerror, only pre-login 401s on /api/me (expected). Seed data (TEST_IMG_Course + 2 docs + TEST_IMG_FE_Course + 1 doc + all pages/figures/generated-doc) cleaned up by module-scoped fixture teardown + explicit script: final counts 0 TEST_ courses, 0 TEST_ docs. Owner emil@jawel.se docs (5) untouched. Total paid AI calls across this iteration: 3 (test_02, test_03, test_04 rescan) + 1 corner-detection call per fresh page = 2 corner + 2 OCR + 1 rescan OCR = within budget.
critical_code_review_comments: imaging.keystone (imaging.py:18-41) correctly orders TL,TR,BR,BL and derives output size from max(TL-TR,BL-BR) width and max(TL-BL,TR-BR) height. The 3% tolerance frame check (line 30) uses sum of normalised dx+dy per corner — correctly skips scans where corners match the image frame within ~30/1000 (~3%). The convexity + 25% minimum-size gate (line 38) is sufficient to reject bad corner answers from the AI without a numeric cross-product; good enough in practice for study-material photos.

imaging.white_balance (imaging.py:44-57) uses the brightest 25% percentile as the paper sample and then median across RGB, scaling to a target of 245.0. The <60 min threshold on the measured white correctly short-circuits dark images (verified by test_02). ImageOps.autocontrast(cutoff=0.5) at the end can shave 1 LSB off the darkest channel, so medians land around 244-245 rather than exactly 245 — tests tolerate this.

imaging.correct_crop (imaging.py:71-81) builds the paper ring with a margin of max(6, 2% of page side) and concatenates top/bottom/left/right strips. Uses `sample` parameter to drive white_balance; falls back to global brightest-25% when the ring has <50 pixels. Correct handling of near-edge crops (slice to 0 on negative index) verified in test_02 of TestCorrectCrop.

pipeline.process_page (pipeline.py:192-256) is idempotent for correction: the `if not page.get('corrected')` gate (line 202) ensures keystone+wb+re-upload happens exactly once per page, so rescan does NOT touch image_url — verified end-to-end in test_04. The OCR path uses the (possibly corrected) `full` bytes for both OCR and figure cropping — correct_crop then white-balances each figure using its surrounding ring. Clean two-stage design.

ai.detect_page_corners (ai.py:300-305) always picks Gemini when available and uses the fast tier (gemini-3.8-flash). The CORNERS_PROMPT returns is_photo_of_page bool + corners; the implementation correctly returns None when is_photo_of_page=false, which cleanly feeds the `corners=None -> wb only` branch in correct_page. Note: no try/except around strip_json — a corrupt JSON from the AI will bubble up as AIError and be caught by the broad `except Exception` in process_page (line 208) which logs and continues with corners=None. Correct.

pipeline.correct_crop import name clash: pipeline.py imports `correct_crop` from imaging and defines no local shadow — crop_and_store (line 99) correctly uses it inside asyncio.to_thread. No sync blocking in the hot path.

No MongoDB `_id` leaks (projections {_id:0} used consistently); env vars only; no hard-coded URLs. The new corrected-page CommHub upload uses the same {page_id}_c.jpg naming convention (pipeline.py:212) — distinct from original {page_id}.jpg so there is no filename collision if commhub_delete fails for the original.

Minor: pipeline.process_page unconditionally resizes the AI input to 2000 px (line 221) regardless of whether the page was corrected or not — this is correct and keeps AI token cost stable even for very large skewed photos.
